tweet_summary: A 21-year-old quote-tweets the viral 'man and parrot' math puzzle with the bit 'i have a PhD in maths from the university of cambridge and i can't solve this' — obvious self-deprecating joke.
why_note_decision: Comments overwhelmingly recognize it as a joke ('Whenever I see an obvious joke tweet... I lose a little bit of remaining faith in humanity'). The puzzle is trivial (basic 2-equation system, parrot=15). The author's bio is '21 [...] occasionally sarcastic, antisocial commentary'. The original note pedantically 'corrects' the credentials with a link to author's profile and Cambridge program directory, which raters rejected as note-not-needed (22) and missing-key-points (14). Showed massive impressions (25.8M) because the joke went viral.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. Tweet is an obvious self-deprecating joke from a 21-year-old quoting a trivial viral math puzzle; the 'I have a Cambridge PhD' framing is the punchline. Any earnest credentials-check note is a false positive on humor.

fact_check.claim_verdict: Joke tweet; literal credential claim not the point.

importance.lens_rationale: Pure joke at huge scale (25.8M impressions) — perfect false-positive trap; not impactful misinfo.
